question: Bind — ATK, 5v5 full-buy, 1:26 left, no spike. You are alone entering B Long, the rest of your team is spread toward A and Mid, no defender has been seen yet. How do you take this space?

options.label: Slice B Long tight against cover, clear one angle at a time, and hold for a teammate before committing deep
options.explication_courte: Map control is the space you can move through safely — you win it by clearing angle-by-angle and only pushing as deep as you can trade. Taking B Long methodically denies the defender a free pick and keeps the whole default flexible (still able to hit A, B, or split).

sources_option.citation: Map control is the set of spaces your team can safely move through; a default takes early space without committing, then decides which site to hit

options.label: Dry-sprint all the way down B Long to Hookah/site to grab the space fast before defenders set up
options.explication_courte: Running into unknown space with no util and no trade behind you hands the defender a free wide-swing pick. You can lose the man AND the space, turning a 5v5 default into a 4v5 with the round plan blown.

sources_option.citation: Taking space recklessly without trades or utility gives it straight back — space is only controlled if you can hold or refrag on it

options.label: Throw your signature to block/deny the B Long angle, then step out under it to secure the first third of the lane
options.explication_courte: Using util to deny the sightline is a valid way to claim space, but spending your signature this early with nobody committing behind you can be premature — you may want it saved for the actual site hit.

sources_option.citation: Utility that cuts a chokepoint's sightline lets attackers claim space, but util spent early is util you don't have for the execute

options.label: Back off B Long entirely and rotate to stack Mid/A with the rest of the team
options.explication_courte: Abandoning B Long for free gives the defense the entire B half of the map and lets them collapse and flank into your Mid/A stack. Ceding a whole lane on a full-buy round with a numbers-even count is throwing away tempo.

sources_option.citation: Giving up a chokepoint without contest hands the defense free rotations and flank timing on your remaining players

explication_longue: This is a pure map-control decision, the layer of Valorant that decides most rounds 20 seconds before any bullet is fired. As the lone attacker in B Long on a full-buy 5v5 default, your job is to claim the space you can actually hold and refrag on — not to win a duel and not to give the lane away. Slicing B Long tight against cover, clearing one angle at a time, and pausing for a teammate before you commit deep is how elite attackers convert territory: you deny the defender a free wide-swing pick, you keep information flowing, and you keep the whole default alive (the team can still choose A, B, or a split once space is banked). Dry-sprinting to site is the classic low-elo mistake — you trade the certainty of controlled space for a coinflip duel with no trade behind you, and losing it costs both the man and the plan. Spending your signature to deny the angle is defensible but often premature; that utility is usually worth more on the actual site execute. Backing off entirely is the worst line: ceding the whole B half for free lets the defense rotate and flank into your Mid/A group. Take the space, don't gamble it, don't give it away.

sources.citation: Map control = space you can safely move through, communicate across, and hold if pushed; defaults bank space before choosing a site
